Available online 8 September 2026. Article 102583; journal pre-proof.

## Summary

The paper examines matching between workers and firms when the surplus from a match is learned through public signals. Posterior beliefs define an assignment game at each date, allowing the analysis of stable allocations as information accumulates. Under a condition ensuring a unique efficient matching, the surplus-maximising matching eventually becomes efficient almost surely, with an exponential bound on the probability of an inefficient match. The analysis also considers how signal precision and industry-specific comparative advantage affect outcomes.
